clauses.statement: An allowlisted Slack user in an allowed channel can invoke /ryoko-develop and the request is acknowledged then dispatched exactly once through the existing internal /develop boundary.
Missing, empty, or non-matching Slack user allowlists fail closed before identity lookups or session dispatch.
Missing, empty, or non-matching development channel allowlists fail closed before Slack lookups or session dispatch.
The SessionManager enforces the same channel boundary so legacy mention-based internal /develop input cannot bypass the Slack command guard.
The generated Slack App Manifest declares the /ryoko-develop command and commands OAuth scope while continuing to use Socket Mode without a public command endpoint.
When the development runner is disabled, /ryoko-develop returns an ephemeral denial and does not dispatch or fall back to another execution path.
Activation requires Slack App reinstall, explicit pilot channel configuration, and gateway restart; rollback disables the runner and requires no data migration.

diagrams.title: Slack native development command flow
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  User[Slack user] --> Command[/ryoko-develop]
  Command --> Ack[Immediate ack]
  Ack --> Guards[User and channel guards]
  Guards --> Session[SessionManager]
  Session --> Runner[Isolated VibePro runner]

diagrams.title: Slack command trust boundaries
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Input[Untrusted Slack input] --> Ack[Immediate ack]
  Ack --> UserGuard{User allowlisted}
  UserGuard -- no --> Deny[Ephemeral denial]
  UserGuard -- yes --> ChannelGuard{Channel allowlisted}
  ChannelGuard -- no --> Deny
  ChannelGuard -- yes --> Dispatch[Session dispatch]
  Dispatch --> Isolated[Isolated runner]
